question: As of March 2023, how many High Courts are there in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 25.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of March 2023, India has 25 High Courts. (भारत के उच्च न्यायालय — 25)

 

• High Courts are established under Article 214 of the Constitution, which states that there shall be a High Court for each State.

 

• The Allahabad High Court (Uttar Pradesh) is the largest High Court by jurisdiction, while the Calcutta High Court (established 1862) is the oldest High Court in India.

 

• Some High Courts have common jurisdiction over more than one State/UT — e.g., the Punjab and Haryana High Court (Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh), the Guwahati High Court (Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh), and the Bombay High Court (Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu).

 

• The Andhra Pradesh High Court at Amaravati (2019) is among the most recently reorganised High Courts, following the state's bifurcation and the creation of a separate Telangana High Court.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 231 empowers Parliament to establish a common High Court for two or more States and/or a Union Territory.

 

• Judges of a High Court are appointed by the President of India under Article 217.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (35), Option 3 (30) and Option 4 (20): These are incorrect numerical distractors; the verified count of High Courts in India, as of March 2023, is 25.

question: Harela is a festival of greenery, peace, prosperity, and environmental conservation, primarily celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Harela is a popular festival of Uttarakhand that celebrates the onset of the monsoon season, greenery, peace, prosperity and environmental conservation. (हरेला पर्व — उत्तराखंड)

 

• It is celebrated twice a year — in Chaitra (mid-March, marking the start of the Hindu New Year) and in Shravan (mid-July, marking the arrival of monsoon); the Shravan Harela is the more widely known.

 

• People sow five or seven types of seeds in a basket about ten days before the festival; the sprouted saplings (also called "Harela") are cut and offered to family elders, who bless the younger generation by placing them on their heads.

 

• Tree plantation is a central ritual of the festival, reflecting its strong ecological and environmental message.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of Uttarakhand include Phool Dei, Ghee Sankranti, and Bikhoti.

 

• Uttarakhand's state government has also declared Harela as a symbol of its afforestation and green cover initiatives.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Notable festivals here include Bhagoria and Namaste Orchha Festival, not Harela.

 

• Haryana (Option 2): Notable festivals here include Teej and Gugga Naumi, not Harela.

 

• Assam (Option 3): Assam celebrates the Bihu festivals (Rongali, Kati and Bhogali), not Harela.

question: Which species is known as black lipped pearl oyster found in the Indo-Pacific, within tropical coral reefs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pinctada margaritifera.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pinctada margaritifera, commonly called the black-lipped pearl oyster, is a species of marine bivalve mollusc found in the tropical waters of the Indo-Pacific region, typically within coral reefs and lagoons. (काली होंठ वाली मोती सीप — Pinctada margaritifera)

 

• It belongs to the family Pteriidae (pearl oysters) and is widely cultivated for producing natural black/dark-coloured pearls, especially famous in Tahiti and French Polynesia.

 

• The species has a distinctive dark, almost black margin along the inner shell (nacre), which gives it its common name.

 

• It is an economically important species for the pearl culture (aquaculture) industry worldwide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bivalve molluscs like oysters are filter feeders and play an important role in maintaining water quality in marine ecosystems.

 

• Other commercially important pearl oyster species include Pinctada fucata and Pinctada maxima.

 

NOTE

 

• Aplysia dactylomela (Option 1): This is a species of sea hare, a marine gastropod (sea slug), not an oyster.

 

• Dentalium neohexagonum (Option 2): This is a species of tusk shell (scaphopod), a tube-shelled marine mollusc, not an oyster.

 

• Chaetopleura apiculata (Option 3): This is a species of chiton, a marine mollusc with a shell of eight overlapping plates, not an oyster.

question: The CSO adopted the concept of Gross Value Added in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is January 2015.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Central Statistics Office (CSO) introduced the new series of national accounts with 2011-12 as the base year and adopted the concept of Gross Value Added (GVA) at basic prices in January 2015. (सकल मूल्य वर्धित — जनवरी 2015)

 

• GVA measures the value of goods and services produced in an economy after deducting the cost of inputs and raw materials, and is calculated as GVA = GDP + subsidies - taxes.

 

• This change brought India's national accounts methodology closer to international best practices, as recommended by the UN System of National Accounts (SNA) 2008.

 

• The CSO functions under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• In 2019, the CSO and the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) were merged to form the National Statistical Office (NSO).

 

• GDP at market prices is derived from GVA by adding product taxes and subtracting product subsidies.

 

NOTE

 

• January 2012, January 2017 and January 2013 (Options 1, 3 and 4): These are incorrect dates; the CSO's adoption of the GVA concept along with the new base year (2011-12) series was officially announced in January 2015.

question: Which of the following social reformers of 19th century India was the author of ‘Stree Purush Tulana’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tarabai Shinde.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tarabai Shinde was a 19th-century Indian social reformer and one of the earliest feminist writers of modern India, who wrote 'Stree Purush Tulana' (A Comparison Between Women and Men) in 1882. (स्त्री पुरुष तुलना — ताराबाई शिंदे)

 

• The book is considered one of the earliest feminist texts in modern Indian literature; it critiqued patriarchy and the double standards applied to men and women in Indian society.

 

• She wrote the book in Marathi, and it was published with the support of the Satyashodhak Samaj, founded by Jyotirao Phule, whose ideas influenced her work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to fight caste discrimination and promote social equality.

 

• Other notable 19th-century women reformers/writers include Savitribai Phule, who worked extensively on women's education.

 

NOTE

 

• Swarnakumari Devi (Option 2): She was a Bengali novelist and social worker, sister of Rabindranath Tagore, known for founding Sakhi Samiti, not for 'Stree Purush Tulana'.

 

• Pandita Ramabai (Option 3): She was a scholar and social reformer known for founding the Arya Mahila Samaj and Sharada Sadan, and for writing 'The High Caste Hindu Woman'.

 

• Usha Mehta (Option 4): She was a freedom fighter known for running the underground Congress Radio during the Quit India Movement, not a 19th-century reformer.

question: How many medals did India win in International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) World Cup 2022, which was held in Cairo, Egypt?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India topped the medal table at the ISSF World Cup 2022, held in Cairo, Egypt, winning a total of 7 medals — 4 gold, 2 silver and 1 bronze. (आईएसएसएफ विश्व कप 2022, काहिरा — भारत 7 पदक)

 

• This was India's best-ever performance at an ISSF World Cup, finishing first in the medal tally, ahead of countries like Hungary and Korea.

 

• Indian shooters such as Rudrankksh Patil, Elavenil Valarivan, Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar and others contributed to this medal haul across rifle and pistol events.

 

• The ISSF (International Shooting Sport Federation) is the world governing body for Olympic shooting sports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has consistently been a strong performer in shooting sports, producing Olympic medallists such as Abhinav Bindra (2008 gold) and multiple World Cup and World Championship medallists.

 

• The National Rifle Association of India (NRAI) governs shooting sports in the country.

 

NOTE

 

• 9, 6 and 8 (Options 1, 2 and 4): These are incorrect medal counts; India's verified tally at the ISSF World Cup 2022 in Cairo was 7 medals.

question: Ustad Vilayat Ali Khan is a maestro in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Vilayat Khan (1928-2004) was one of the greatest sitar maestros of Hindustani classical music, renowned for pioneering the vocal-style "gayaki ang" of sitar playing. (सितार वादक — उस्ताद विलायत खान)

 

• He belonged to the Imdadkhani (Etawah) gharana of sitar playing, a lineage passed down through his family.

 

• He famously declined the Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan awards on more than one occasion, feeling the honours were not appropriately timed or recognised.

 

• His sons, Shujaat Khan and Hidayat Khan, have carried forward the sitar tradition of the gharana.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other legendary sitar players of India include Pandit Ravi Shankar, founder of a rival but equally celebrated tradition of sitar playing.

 

• The sitar is a plucked stringed instrument central to Hindustani classical music, believed to have evolved from instruments like the veena.

 

NOTE

 

• Tabla (Option 1): Legendary tabla maestros include Ustad Zakir Hussain and Ustad Alla Rakha, not Vilayat Khan.

 

• Mridangam (Option 2): This is a percussion instrument central to Carnatic music, associated with maestros like Palghat Mani Iyer.

 

• Flute (Option 4): Renowned Indian flute (bansuri) maestros include Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, not Vilayat Khan.

question: Which physical feature of India prevents the cold winds from central Asia from entering the Indian subcontinents?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himalayas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Himalayas, forming India's northern mountain wall, act as a climatic barrier that prevents the bitterly cold winds from Central Asia from entering the Indian subcontinent, keeping the Indian plains relatively warmer in winter. (हिमालय पर्वत — जलवायु अवरोधक)

 

• The Himalayas also intercept the monsoon winds coming from the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea, forcing them to shed most of their moisture over the Indian subcontinent, which is crucial for India's rainfall pattern.

 

• Stretching about 2,400 km, the Himalayas run across India's northern border from Jammu & Kashmir to Arunachal Pradesh, and are the world's youngest and highest fold mountain range.

 

• They are geologically classified into three parallel ranges: the Himadri (Greater Himalayas), Himachal (Lesser Himalayas), and Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Himalayas are also the source of major perennial rivers of India, including the Ganga, Yamuna, and Brahmaputra.

 

• Mount Everest (Sagarmatha), the world's highest peak, lies in the Himalayan range on the Nepal-China border.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian plains (Option 1): The Indo-Gangetic plains are formed by alluvial deposits and do not act as a wind barrier.

 

• Indian desert (Option 2): The Thar Desert lies in the west and is unrelated to blocking cold winds from Central Asia.

 

• Coastal area (Option 3): India's coastal areas moderate temperature through maritime influence, but do not block Central Asian winds.

question: Which state initiated the implementation of the Mid-day Meal scheme in elementary schools?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tamil Nadu was the pioneering state in India to implement a Mid-day Meal scheme in elementary schools, starting with a nutritious meal programme in 1956, later expanded state-wide as a universal programme in 1982 under Chief Minister M. G. Ramachandran. (मध्याह्न भोजन योजना — तमिलनाडु)

 

• The scheme aimed to improve school enrolment, retention, and nutritional status of children while combating classroom hunger.

 

• Inspired by Tamil Nadu's success, the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE), popularly called the Mid-Day Meal Scheme, was launched nationally by the Government of India in 1995.

 

• The scheme is now known as PM POSHAN (PM Poshan Shakti Nirman), renamed in 2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mid-Day Meal Scheme is one of the world's largest school feeding programmes, covering crores of children across government and government-aided schools.

 

• The scheme falls under the Ministry of Education, Government of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka (Options 2, 3 and 4): While these states later implemented the mid-day meal programme as part of the national scheme, they were not the pioneering state; Tamil Nadu was the first to introduce it.

question: In the 7th Century AD, a new religion called Islam was born in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arabia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Islam originated in Arabia (present-day Saudi Arabia) in the 7th century AD, founded by Prophet Muhammad, who began receiving revelations around 610 CE in the city of Mecca. (इस्लाम धर्म — अरब)

 

• The two holiest cities of Islam, Mecca and Medina, are both located in the Arabian Peninsula.

 

• The Islamic calendar (Hijri calendar) begins from 622 CE, the year of the Hijra — Prophet Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina.

 

• The central religious text of Islam is the Quran, believed by Muslims to be the word of God as revealed to Muhammad.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Islam later spread widely to regions including Persia, Central Asia, North Africa, and South and Southeast Asia including India, Malaysia and Indonesia.

 

• Indonesia today has the world's largest Muslim population, though Islam did not originate there.

 

NOTE

 

• Malaysia, South Africa and Indonesia (Options 1, 2 and 4): Islam later spread to and became prominent in these regions, but it did not originate there; it originated in Arabia.

question: Who among the following freedom fighters of India is the author of the book, ‘The Indian Struggle’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhas Chandra Bose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose authored the book 'The Indian Struggle', first published in 1935, which covers the history of the Indian independence movement from 1920 to 1934. (भारतीय संघर्ष — सुभाष चंद्र बोस)

 

• Bose founded the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) and gave the famous call "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom".

 

• He also served as the President of the Indian National Congress twice, in 1938 (Haripura session) and 1939 (Tripuri session).

 

• He established the Azad Hind Government (Provisional Government of Free India) in 1943 at Singapore.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bose's other notable works include 'An Indian Pilgrim', his unfinished autobiography.

 

• He is popularly known as 'Netaji', and his disappearance/death in 1945 near Taipei remains a subject of historical debate.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahatma Gandhi (Option 1): His notable works include 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' and 'Hind Swaraj', not 'The Indian Struggle'.

 

• Motilal Nehru (Option 2): He was a prominent Congress leader known for the Nehru Report (1928), not for authoring 'The Indian Struggle'.

 

• Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 3): Known as the 'Iron Man of India' for integrating princely states, he did not author 'The Indian Struggle'.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions about the organisation of ‘Village Panchayats’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 40.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 40 of the Indian Constitution, under the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV), directs the State to take steps to organise Village Panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government. (ग्राम पंचायत — अनुच्छेद 40)

 

• This directive laid the constitutional foundation for the later 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which gave Panchayati Raj Institutions constitutional status via Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule.

 

• The 73rd Amendment established a three-tier Panchayati Raj system: Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block/intermediate level), and Zila Parishad (district level).

 

• Directive Principles of State Policy, though not enforceable by courts, are considered fundamental in the governance of the country as per Article 37.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of Panchayati Raj was inspired by Mahatma Gandhi's vision of Gram Swaraj (village self-rule).

 

• The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended the three-tier Panchayati Raj system, first adopted by Rajasthan in 1959.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 31 (Option 1): Originally dealt with the Right to Property, later omitted as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment.

 

• Article 38 (Option 2): Directs the State to secure a social order for the promotion of the welfare of the people.

 

• Article 36 (Option 3): Provides the definition of 'State' for the purposes of Part IV (Directive Principles).

question: Sitar maestro, Pandit Ravi Shankar was awarded which of the following awards by the Government of India in 1999?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat Ratna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar, the legendary sitar maestro, was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1999. (भारत रत्न — पंडित रवि शंकर)

 

• He is widely credited with popularising Hindustani classical music and the sitar internationally, including through his collaborations with violinist Yehudi Menuhin and Beatles guitarist George Harrison.

 

• Ravi Shankar had earlier also received the Padma Bhushan (1967) and the Padma Vibhushan (1981), making the Bharat Ratna his final and highest civilian honour.

 

• He is the father of Grammy-winning musician Anoushka Shankar and singer Norah Jones.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Bharat Ratna awardees from the field of music/arts include M. S. Subbulakshmi (1998), Bismillah Khan (2001), and Lata Mangeshkar (2001).

 

• The Bharat Ratna was instituted in 1954 and can be awarded posthumously since 1955.

 

NOTE

 

• Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan (Options 1, 2 and 4): These are lower-ranking civilian awards than the Bharat Ratna; Ravi Shankar had already received the Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan in earlier years, but in 1999 he specifically received the Bharat Ratna.

question: ‘Au’ is the symbol for which of the following elements?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gold.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The chemical symbol 'Au' stands for Gold, derived from its Latin name 'Aurum', meaning "shining dawn" or "glow of sunrise". (स्वर्ण/सोना — Au)

 

• Gold has the atomic number 79 and is a dense, soft, malleable and ductile transition metal, prized for its lustre and resistance to corrosion.

 

• It is widely used in jewellery, electronics, and as a store of value/currency reserve by central banks worldwide.

 

• Gold occurs naturally in a metallic form and is one of the least chemically reactive elements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Latin-derived chemical symbols include Fe (Ferrum) for Iron, Na (Natrium) for Sodium, and Ag (Argentum) for Silver.

 

• India is one of the largest consumers of gold in the world, primarily for jewellery and investment purposes.

 

NOTE

 

• Aluminium (Option 2): Its chemical symbol is Al, not Au.

 

• Silver (Option 3): Its chemical symbol is Ag (from Latin 'Argentum'), not Au.

 

• Argon (Option 4): Its chemical symbol is Ar, not Au.

question: Which of the following options is associated with the class of cold-blooded animals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chameleon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The chameleon is a type of lizard, belonging to the class Reptilia, and reptiles are cold-blooded (ectothermic) animals whose body temperature depends on the external environment. (शीत रक्त वाले जीव — गिरगिट)

 

• Ectothermic animals cannot internally regulate their body temperature and rely on behaviour, such as basking in the sun, to warm up.

 

• Chameleons are especially well known for their ability to change skin colour, largely for communication and temperature regulation rather than pure camouflage as commonly believed.

 

• Other examples of cold-blooded animals include snakes, frogs, turtles, and fish.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Warm-blooded (endothermic) animals, such as birds and mammals, can maintain a constant internal body temperature regardless of their surroundings.

 

• Reptiles, being ectothermic, generally have lower metabolic rates than birds and mammals of similar size.

 

NOTE

 

• Pavo (Option 2): This is the scientific genus name for peafowl (peacock), a bird, and birds are warm-blooded.

 

• Macropus (Option 3): This is the scientific genus name for kangaroos, a mammal, and mammals are warm-blooded.

 

• Psittacula (Option 4): This is the scientific genus name for a group of parakeets, a bird, and birds are warm-blooded.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India grants power to the President to appoint Judges of the Supreme Court?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 124(2).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 124(2) of the Indian Constitution empowers the President of India to appoint the Judges of the Supreme Court, in consultation with such Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts as the President may deem necessary. (सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों की नियुक्ति — अनुच्छेद 124(2))

 

• The Chief Justice of India must always be consulted in the appointment of other Supreme Court judges.

 

• Appointments today follow the collegium system, evolved through Supreme Court judgments (the "Judges Cases"), which is not explicitly mentioned in the Constitution's text.

 

• A Supreme Court judge holds office until the age of 65 years, as provided under the same Article.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 124 as a whole deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court.

 

• Judges of High Courts, similarly, are appointed by the President under Article 217.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 123(1) (Option 2): This deals with the President's power to promulgate Ordinances when Parliament is not in session, not judicial appointments.

 

• Article 127(3) (Option 3): This relates to provisions for appointing ad hoc judges to the Supreme Court.

 

• Article 128(4) (Option 4): This relates to the attendance of retired judges at sittings of the Supreme Court.

question: In which year was the International Olympic Committee formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1894.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Olympic Committee (IOC) was founded on 23 June 1894 in Paris, France, by Baron Pierre de Coubertin, who is regarded as the father of the modern Olympic Games. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय ओलंपिक समिति — 1894)

 

• The IOC's formation led directly to the organisation of the first modern Olympic Games in Athens, Greece, in 1896.

 

• The IOC is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

• The IOC is responsible for organising the summer and winter Olympic Games and upholding the Olympic Charter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Olympic motto is "Citius, Altius, Fortius" (Faster, Higher, Stronger), later extended to "— Communiter" (Together).

 

• India's Olympic body is the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), formed in 1927.

 

NOTE

 

• 1896 (Option 1): This is the year of the first modern Olympic Games (Athens), not the founding year of the IOC itself.

 

• 1892 and 1898 (Options 2 and 3): These are incorrect years; the IOC was formed in 1894.

question: To which group do the alkaline earth metals such as radium, barium and strontium belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Group 2A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alkaline earth metals — beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium and radium — belong to Group 2 (Group 2A/ IIA) of the modern Periodic Table. (क्षारीय मृदा धातु — समूह 2A)

 

• These elements have two electrons in their outermost shell, giving them a valency of +2 and making them highly reactive, though less reactive than the alkali metals of Group 1.

 

• They are generally silvery-white, relatively soft metals that react with water (though less vigorously than alkali metals) to form hydroxides and hydrogen gas.

 

• Radium is also notably radioactive, discovered by Marie Curie and Pierre Curie.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Group 1 (Group 1A) elements are called alkali metals (lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium, francium).

 

• Calcium and magnesium, also alkaline earth metals, are essential nutrients for the human body (bones and muscles respectively).

 

NOTE

 

• Group 5A (Option 1): This group (nitrogen family/pnictogens) includes nitrogen and phosphorus, not the alkaline earth metals.

 

• Group 1A (Option 3): This group consists of the alkali metals, not the alkaline earth metals.

 

• Group 3A (Option 4): This group (boron family) includes boron and aluminium, not the alkaline earth metals.

question: In which of the following games is one player known as the Wicketkeeper?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cricket.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Wicketkeeper is a specialist fielding position in Cricket, positioned directly behind the batsman's wicket, responsible for stopping deliveries missed by the batsman, catching, stumping and run-outs. (विकेटकीपर — क्रिकेट)

 

• The wicketkeeper is the only fielder permitted to wear gloves and leg pads in the field, apart from the batsman.

 

• Famous Indian wicketkeepers include Mahendra Singh Dhoni and Rishabh Pant.

 

• Cricket is played between two teams of 11 players each, using a bat and ball, on a field with a central 22-yard pitch.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cricket's major formats include Test cricket, One Day Internationals (ODIs), and Twenty20 (T20).

 

• The sport is governed internationally by the International Cricket Council (ICC), headquartered in Dubai.

 

NOTE

 

• Football (Option 1): The equivalent guarding position is called a Goalkeeper, not Wicketkeeper.

 

• Basketball (Option 2): Player positions include Point Guard, Center and Forward; there is no Wicketkeeper role.

 

• Hockey (Option 4): The equivalent guarding position is called a Goalkeeper, not Wicketkeeper.

question: Which of the following is the transboundary river between India and Pakistan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ravi River, one of the five rivers of Punjab, originates in the Himalayas in India and flows through Jammu and Kashmir and Punjab before entering Pakistan, ultimately merging with the Chenab River, making it a key transboundary river between India and Pakistan. (रावी नदी — भारत-पाकिस्तान सीमापार नदी)

 

• Under the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), the waters of the Ravi, Beas and Sutlej (the "Eastern Rivers") were allocated for the unrestricted use of India, though the Ravi still physically flows onward into Pakistani territory.

 

• The Ravi is historically significant — the city of Lahore in Pakistan is situated on its banks.

 

• It is part of the larger Indus river system, along with the Jhelum, Chenab, Beas and Sutlej.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indus Waters Treaty allocated the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab (the "Western Rivers") largely for Pakistan's use, with limited use permitted to India.

 

• The treaty was brokered by the World Bank and signed by Indian PM Jawaharlal Nehru and Pakistani President Ayub Khan.

 

NOTE

 

• Indus (Option 1) and Jhelum (Option 4): While these rivers also flow between India and Pakistan, they are designated as the "Western Rivers" under the Indus Waters Treaty, allocated mainly to Pakistan's use; the intended answer here is the Ravi.

 

• Beas (Option 3): The Beas River flows entirely within Indian territory (Himachal Pradesh and Punjab) and joins the Sutlej without crossing into Pakistan, so it is not a transboundary river with Pakistan.

question: According to the Agricultural and Processed food products Export Development Authority (APEDA) 2020-2021, which state of India has the first rank in grapes production?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per APEDA data for 2020-21, Maharashtra ranks first in grapes production in India, contributing the largest share of the country's total output. (अंगूर उत्पादन — महाराष्ट्र प्रथम)

 

• The Nashik district of Maharashtra is often called the "Grape City/Wine Capital of India", being the hub of both table grape and wine grape cultivation.

 

• Maharashtra also leads in India's grape exports, primarily to Europe and other overseas markets, and is a major centre for the Indian wine industry.

 

• Karnataka is generally the second-largest grape-producing state in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• APEDA was established under the APEDA Act, 1985, and functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, promoting export of agricultural and processed food products.

 

• India is among the top grape-producing countries in the world, with cultivation concentrated in the western and southern states.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (Options 2, 3 and 4): These states produce grapes on a smaller scale and do not hold the first rank; Maharashtra is the top producer as per APEDA 2020-21 data.

question: Gautamiputra Satakarni titled Rajaraja and Maharaja is related to which of the following dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satavahana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gautamiputra Satakarni was the most illustrious ruler of the Satavahana dynasty, who took titles such as "Rajaraja" and "Maharaja", and reigned in the 1st-2nd century CE. (सातवाहन वंश — गौतमीपुत्र सातकर्णी)

 

• He is credited with defeating the Western Kshatrapas (Shaka ruler Nahapana) and restoring Satavahana power in the Deccan, as recorded in the Nashik Prashasti inscription issued by his mother, Gautami Balashri.

 

• The Satavahanas ruled over large parts of the Deccan and central India, with their capital initially at Pratishthana (Paithan).

 

• Gautamiputra Satakarni also called himself "Ekabrahmana" (the unique Brahmin) and claimed to have destroyed the pride of Kshatriyas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Satavahanas were also known as the Andhras, and were significant patrons of Buddhism, including at sites like Amaravati.

 

• Satavahana coins provide valuable information about their rulers and are among the earliest Indian coins to bear royal portraits.

 

NOTE

 

• Shunga (Option 1): This dynasty, founded by Pushyamitra Shunga after overthrowing the Mauryas, ruled North India, unrelated to Gautamiputra Satakarni.

 

• Pandya (Option 2): This was an ancient Tamil dynasty of South India, with capital at Madurai, unrelated to Gautamiputra Satakarni.

 

• Shaka (Option 4): The Shakas (Western Kshatrapas), particularly Nahapana, were actually defeated by Gautamiputra Satakarni, not the dynasty he belonged to.

question: Which of the following has the highest salinity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dead sea.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dead Sea, a salt lake bordered by Jordan, Israel and the West Bank, has a salinity of approximately 34%, making it one of the saltiest water bodies on Earth and roughly 9-10 times saltier than the open ocean. (मृत सागर — सर्वाधिक लवणता)

 

• Its extreme salinity, caused by high evaporation with no outlet, makes the water dense enough for objects and people to float easily, and supports almost no aquatic life — hence the name "Dead" Sea.

 

• The Dead Sea's shoreline, at about 430 metres below sea level, is the lowest point on Earth's land surface.

 

• It is fed primarily by the Jordan River and has no outflow, leading to continuous concentration of dissolved salts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Great Salt Lake in Utah, USA, has a variable salinity ranging roughly from 5% to 27% depending on water levels, generally lower than the Dead Sea.

 

• The Red Sea, one of the saltiest open seas, has a salinity of about 4%, while Lake Van in Turkey, the world's largest soda lake, has a comparatively moderate salinity of roughly 3-4%.

 

NOTE

 

• Great salt lake (Option 1): Though highly saline and sometimes cited for extreme salinity at low water levels, its typical/average salinity remains lower than the Dead Sea's.

 

• Lake Van (Option 2): This is a large soda (alkaline) lake in Turkey with moderate salinity, far lower than the Dead Sea; it is not the correct answer despite being marked in the source key.

 

• Red sea (Option 3): While saltier than the average ocean, its salinity (~4%) is far lower than that of the Dead Sea.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution contains Fundamental Duties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 51A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A of the Indian Constitution, inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, lays down the Fundamental Duties of every citizen of India. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• Originally 10 Fundamental Duties were listed; an 11th duty — the duty of parents/guardians to provide educational opportunities to children aged 6-14 — was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• Fundamental Duties were included based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee and are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

 

• Like Directive Principles, Fundamental Duties are not directly enforceable by courts, but serve as a constant reminder to citizens of their obligations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are listed under Part IVA of the Constitution, a part added specifically by the 42nd Amendment.

 

• One key Fundamental Duty is to "protect and improve the natural environment" and to develop scientific temper and humanism.

 

NOTE

 

• 32A, 45A and 62B (Options 1, 2 and 4): These are not valid/existing Constitutional Article numbers relevant to Fundamental Duties; the correct provision is Article 51A.

question: Mohiniyattam is associated with which of the following traditional dance styles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lasya style.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam, the classical dance form of Kerala, is characterised by the graceful, feminine "Lasya" style of movement, as opposed to the vigorous, masculine "Tandava" style. (मोहिनीअट्टम — लास्य शैली)

 

• The name "Mohiniyattam" literally means "dance of the enchantress", referring to Lord Vishnu's mythological form as Mohini.

 

• It is traditionally a solo dance performed by women, featuring swaying body movements, gentle footwork, and eye and hand gestures (mudras) rooted in the Natya Shastra and Hastha Lakshanadeepika.

 

• The dance is accompanied by Carnatic music, and the songs are typically composed in Malayalam mixed with Sanskrit (Manipravalam).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mohiniyattam was revived and popularised in the 20th century by poet Vallathol Narayana Menon, who also founded the Kerala Kalamandalam.

 

• Kerala's other major classical performance art, Kathakali, in contrast, emphasises the more vigorous Tandava style.

 

NOTE

 

• Samapadam (Option 1): This refers to a basic standing posture/stance in classical Indian dance, not a broad dance style category.

 

• Tribhanga (Option 2): This refers to a graceful three-bend body posture seen in dances like Odissi, not the defining style category of Mohiniyattam.

 

• Chowk (Option 3): This refers to a wide-legged, masculine stance associated with dances like Odissi, representing more vigorous movement, not Mohiniyattam's style.
